"ROLE
You are a senior full-stack + ML engineer. Build a complete, working, 100% free AI Video @COMMENT_BODY@ Voice Dubbing web app, modeled on Sarvam Indus Creator Studio's \"Dubbing\" feature. No paid APIs, no API keys, no credit card. Everything must run on free/open-source tools.

GOAL
User uploads a video/audio file, picks source language and one or more target languages, and gets back a dubbed video (MP4), dubbed audio (MP3), and subtitles (SRT), with the original background music preserved and timing matched.

TECH STACK (free only)
- Frontend: Next.js + Tailwind, mobile-first, clean white UI, collapsible sidebar
- Backend: Python FastAPI, background worker (Celery + Redis, or simple threaded queue), SQLite
- Audio extraction and merge: FFmpeg
- Vocal/background split: Demucs
- Speech-to-text: faster-whisper (word timestamps, language auto-detect)
- Speaker detection: pyannote.audio (fallback: user-selected 1-5 speakers)
- Translation: IndicTrans2 for Indian languages, NLLB-200 as fallback
- Text-to-speech: edge-tts (primary, free), AI4Bharat Indic-Parler-TTS (offline option)
- Voice cloning (optional toggle): OpenVoice or XTTS-v2
- Time fitting: FFmpeg atempo / pyrubberband
- Hosting: Hugging Face Spaces / Render free tier; GPU work on Google Colab + ngrok

LANGUAGES
Hindi, Kannada, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, Marathi, Bengali, Gujarati, Punjabi, Odia, Urdu, English (source auto-detect + multi-select targets).

PAGES
1. Dubbing dashboard
   - Sidebar: Home, Text to Speech, Dubbing, Voice Library, Voice Cloning, Speech to Text, Usage, Docs
   - Top bar: free minutes left, feedback button, \"+\" new dub button
   - Table: thumbnail, name, source language, target language chip, created date, status badge (Queued / Processing / Completed / Failed), download menu
   - Search box, status filter, pagination (\"1-7 of N\")
2. \"Create a dub\" modal
   - Upload / Record tabs (drag-and-drop; max 2GB or 1 hour)
   - Source language (with Auto-detect), number of speakers (1-5), multi-select target languages
   - Advanced options: keep background music, voice cloning on/off, voice gender, speech speed, burn-in subtitles, glossary of words to keep untranslated
   - Cancel and Create dub buttons
3. Progress screen: live steps (Extract audio, Separate vocals, Transcribe, Translate, Generate voice, Sync, Merge) with percentage and ETA
4. Result page: player with Original / Dubbed toggle, side-by-side editable transcript and translation, per-segment \"Regenerate voice\", downloads (MP4, MP3, SRT, VTT)
5. Usage page: free minutes used/left (30 min/day, resets daily)

PIPELINE
upload, then FFmpeg extract audio, then Demucs split (vocals/background), then faster-whisper transcript with timestamps, then merge into sentence segments, then translate each segment with context, then TTS per segment, then time-stretch each clip to fit its original slot (max 1.25x, else shorten the translation), then mix with background at the original loudness, then mux into the video, then save and notify.

QUALITY RULES
- Keep names, brands, and numbers correct; support a do-not-translate glossary
- No clipping or overlapping speech; normalize loudness (-16 LUFS)
- Keep lip/pause timing natural; preserve silence gaps
- Process long files in chunks so the free tier does not time out
- Clear error messages and retry on failure; delete temp files after processing

NON-FUNCTIONAL
- Fully responsive for phone screens (touch-friendly, large buttons)
- Dark/light toggle
- Rate limit: 30 free minutes/day per user (cookie or simple login)
- Add a consent checkbox for voice cloning (\"I have the rights to this voice\")

DELIVERABLES
1. Folder structure
2. Complete backend and frontend code (no placeholders, no \"TODO\")
3. requirements.txt, package.json, Dockerfile, .env.example
4. Step-by-step local setup + free deployment guide (Hugging Face Spaces / Render / Colab)
5. A Gradio single-file MVP first, so I can test the pipeline immediately, then the full UI

BUILD ORDER
Step 1: working Gradio MVP of the pipeline. Step 2: FastAPI backend. Step 3: dashboard, modal, progress, result pages. Step 4: usage limits and polish. After each step, tell me how to run and test it.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

"""Local, free-to-run video dubbing MVP (Gradio).

Pipeline: FFmpeg -> optional Demucs -> faster-whisper -> NLLB-200 -> edge-tts
-> time fitting/mix -> FFmpeg MP4 mux. Models are downloaded on first use.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
import uuid
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Iterator

import gradio as gr

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
OUTPUT_DIR = Path(os.getenv("OUTPUT_DIR", ROOT / "outputs")).resolve()
OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
MAX_SECONDS = 3600
LANGUAGES = {
    "Hindi": ("hin_Deva", "hi-IN-SwaraNeural", "hi"),
    "Kannada": ("kan_Knda", "kn-IN-SapnaNeural", "kn"),
    "Tamil": ("tam_Taml", "ta-IN-PallaviNeural", "ta"),
    "Telugu": ("tel_Telu", "te-IN-ShrutiNeural", "te"),
    "Malayalam": ("mal_Mlym", "ml-IN-SobhanaNeural", "ml"),
    "Marathi": ("mar_Deva", "mr-IN-AarohiNeural", "mr"),
    "Bengali": ("ben_Beng", "bn-IN-TanishaaNeural", "bn"),
    "Gujarati": ("guj_Gujr", "gu-IN-DhwaniNeural", "gu"),
    "Punjabi": ("pan_Guru", "pa-IN-VaaniNeural", "pa"),
    "Odia": ("ory_Orya", "or-IN-SubhasiniNeural", "or"),
    "Urdu": ("urd_Arab", "ur-PK-UzmaNeural", "ur"),
    "English": ("eng_Latn", "en-US-AriaNeural", "en"),
}
# NLLB uses FLORES-200 language identifiers.
NLLB_CODES = {
    "eng": "eng_Latn", "hin": "hin_Deva", "kan": "kan_Knda", "tam": "tam_Taml",
    "tel": "tel_Telu", "mal": "mal_Mlym", "mar": "mar_Deva", "ben": "ben_Beng",
    "guj": "guj_Gujr", "pan": "pan_Guru", "ory": "ory_Orya", "urd": "urd_Arab",
    "spa": "spa_Latn", "fra": "fra_Latn", "deu": "deu_Latn", "ita": "ita_Latn",
    "por": "por_Latn", "rus": "rus_Cyrl", "zho": "zho_Hans", "jpn": "jpn_Jpan",
    "kor": "kor_Hang", "ara": "arb_Arab", "nld": "nld_Latn", "tur": "tur_Latn",
}


def _run(command: list[str], *, timeout: int | None = None) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
    except FileNotFoundError as exc:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Required program not found: {command[0]}. Install FFmpeg and add it to PATH.") from exc
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as exc:
        raise RuntimeError("A media processing step timed out. Try a shorter file or a machine with more memory.") from exc
    if result.returncode:
        detail = (result.stderr or result.stdout)[-2500:]
        raise RuntimeError(f"Command failed ({command[0]}):\n{detail}")
    return result


def _duration(path: str | Path) -> float:
    result = _run([
        "ffprobe", "-v", "error", "-show_entries", "format=duration", "-of", "default=noprint_wrappers=1:nokey=1", str(path)
    ])
    try:
        duration = float(result.stdout.strip())
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise RuntimeError("Could not read the media duration. Check that the uploaded file is valid.") from exc
    if duration <= 0 or duration > MAX_SECONDS:
        raise RuntimeError("Files must be longer than zero and no more than 60 minutes.")
    return duration


def _has_video(path: str | Path) -> bool:
    result = _run(["ffprobe", "-v", "error", "-select_streams", "v:0", "-show_entries", "stream=codec_type", "-of", "csv=p=0", str(path)])
    return bool(result.stdout.strip())


def _transcribe(audio_path: Path, model_name: str, language: str):
    from faster_whisper import WhisperModel

    compute = os.getenv("WHISPER_COMPUTE_TYPE", "int8")
    device = os.getenv("WHISPER_DEVICE", "cpu")
    model = WhisperModel(model_name, device=device, compute_type=compute)
    selected = None if language == "Auto-detect" else language
    segments, info = model.transcribe(str(audio_path), language=selected, word_timestamps=True, vad_filter=True)
    # Consume the lazy generator while the model is in scope.
    raw = [(float(s.start), float(s.end), (s.text or "").strip()) for s in segments if (s.text or "").strip()]
    return raw, info.language


def _sentence_segments(raw: list[tuple[float, float, str]], duration: float):
    """Merge Whisper chunks into sentence-sized dubbing slots without overlap."""
    merged: list[list[float | str]] = []
    for start, end, text in raw:
        start = max(0.0, min(start, duration))
        end = max(start + 0.05, min(end, duration))
        if merged and not re.search(r"[.!?。！？…]$", str(merged[-1][2])) and start - float(merged[-1][1]) < 0.8:
            merged[-1][1] = max(float(merged[-1][1]), end)
            merged[-1][2] = (str(merged[-1][2]) + " " + text).strip()
        else:
            merged.append([start, end, text])
    clean = []
    previous_end = 0.0
    for start, end, text in merged:
        start = max(float(start), previous_end)
        end = max(start + 0.08, float(end))
        end = min(duration, end)
        if end > start and str(text).strip():
            clean.append((start, end, str(text).strip()))
            previous_end = end
    return clean


_TRANSLATOR = None


def _get_translator():
    global _TRANSLATOR
    if _TRANSLATOR is None:
        from transformers import AutoModelForSeq2SeqLM, AutoTokenizer
        import torch

        name = os.getenv("TRANSLATION_MODEL", "facebook/nllb-200-distilled-600M")
        _TRANSLATOR = (AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(name), AutoModelForSeq2SeqLM.from_pretrained(name), torch)
    return _TRANSLATOR


def _translate_piece(text: str, source_code: str, target_code: str) -> str:
    if not text.strip():
        return text
    tokenizer, model, torch = _get_translator()
    tokenizer.src_lang = source_code
    inputs = tokenizer(text, return_tensors="pt", truncation=True, max_length=512)
    target_id = tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids(target_code)
    with torch.inference_mode():
        output = model.generate(**inputs, forced_bos_token_id=target_id, max_new_tokens=256, num_beams=3)
    return tokenizer.batch_decode(output, skip_special_tokens=True)[0].strip()


def _translate(text: str, source_code: str, target_code: str, glossary: list[str]) -> str:
    # Translate around glossary matches rather than asking the model to copy names/numbers.
    terms = [term.strip() for term in glossary if term.strip()]
    if not terms:
        return _translate_piece(text, source_code, target_code)
    pattern = re.compile("(" + "|".join(re.escape(t) for t in sorted(terms, key=len, reverse=True)) + ")", re.IGNORECASE)
    chunks = pattern.split(text)
    result = []
    for chunk in chunks:
        if not chunk:
            continue
        if pattern.fullmatch(chunk):
            result.append(chunk)
        else:
            translated = _translate_piece(chunk, source_code, target_code)
            result.append(translated if translated else chunk)
    return " ".join(part for part in result if part).strip()


def _edge_voice(text: str, voice: str, rate: int, output_path: Path):
    import edge_tts

    async def save():
        await edge_tts.Communicate(text, voice, rate=f"{rate:+d}%").save(str(output_path))

    asyncio.run(save())


def _srt_time(seconds: float) -> str:
    millis = max(0, round(seconds * 1000))
    hours, millis = divmod(millis, 3_600_000)
    minutes, millis = divmod(millis, 60_000)
    seconds_i, millis = divmod(millis, 1000)
    return f"{hours:02}:{minutes:02}:{seconds_i:02},{millis:03}"


def _write_subtitles(rows, path: Path, vtt: bool = False):
    blocks = []
    for index, (start, end, _, translated) in enumerate(rows, 1):
        begin = _srt_time(start).replace(",", ".") if vtt else _srt_time(start)
        finish = _srt_time(end).replace(",", ".") if vtt else _srt_time(end)
        blocks.append(f"{index if not vtt else ''}\n{begin} --> {finish}\n{translated}")
    path.write_text(("WEBVTT\n\n" if vtt else "") + "\n\n".join(blocks) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")


def dub_media(media_file, target_language: str, source_language: str, speaker_gender: str,
              speech_speed: int, keep_music: bool, glossary_text: str, whisper_model: str) -> Iterator:
    """Gradio generator: yields progress text and then all deliverables."""
    if media_file is None:
        yield "Upload a video or audio file first.", None, None, None, None, None
        return
    source_path = Path(media_file)
    if not source_path.is_file():
        yield "The uploaded file is no longer available. Please upload it again.", None, None, None, None, None
        return
    if target_language not in LANGUAGES:
        yield "Select a supported target language.", None, None, None, None, None
        return

    job_dir = OUTPUT_DIR / uuid.uuid4().hex
    job_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    temp_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="dub-")).resolve()
    try:
        yield "**1/7 — Extracting audio…**", None, None, None, None, None
        duration = _duration(source_path)
        audio = temp_dir / "source.wav"
        _run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-i", str(source_path), "-vn", "-ac", "1", "-ar", "16000", "-c:a", "pcm_s16le", str(audio)], timeout=900)

        background = None
        if keep_music:
            yield "**2/7 — Separating vocals and background (Demucs)…** First run downloads model weights.", None, None, None, None, None
            demucs_out = temp_dir / "separated"
            _run([os.getenv("PYTHON", "python"), "-m", "demucs", "--two-stems=vocals", "-n", "htdemucs", "-o", str(demucs_out), str(source_path)], timeout=7200)
            candidates = list(demucs_out.glob("**/no_vocals.wav"))
            if not candidates:
                raise RuntimeError("Demucs finished but its background stem was not found. Try disabling background preservation.")
            background = candidates[0]

        yield "**3/7 — Transcribing speech with word timestamps…**", None, None, None, None, None
        raw, detected = _transcribe(audio, whisper_model, source_language)
        segments = _sentence_segments(raw, duration)
        if not segments:
            raise RuntimeError("No speech was detected. Try a clearer recording or another Whisper model.")

        source_code = NLLB_CODES.get(detected)
        if not source_code:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Detected language '{detected}' is not supported by the included NLLB model. Select a supported source language or provide a different recording.")
        target_code, base_voice, _ = LANGUAGES[target_language]
        voice = base_voice
        if speaker_gender == "Male":
            voice_map = {"Hindi": "hi-IN-MadhurNeural", "Kannada": "kn-IN-GaganNeural", "Tamil": "ta-IN-ValluvarNeural", "Telugu": "te-IN-MohanNeural", "English": "en-US-GuyNeural"}
            voice = voice_map.get(target_language, base_voice)
        glossary = [t.strip() for t in re.split(r"[,\n]", glossary_text or "") if t.strip()]

        yield "**4/7 — Translating segments…** The first run downloads the open translation model (~2.5 GB).", None, None, None, None, None
        translated_rows = []
        for start, end, original in segments:
            translated = _translate(original, source_code, target_code, glossary)
            translated_rows.append((start, end, original, translated or original))

        yield "**5/7 — Generating target speech…** edge-tts requires an internet connection and is free to use.", None, None, None, None, None
        from pydub import AudioSegment
        from pydub.effects import normalize

        speech_track = AudioSegment.silent(duration=round(duration * 1000), frame_rate=24000).set_channels(1)
        for index, (start, end, _, translated) in enumerate(translated_rows):
            generated = temp_dir / f"voice-{index:05}.mp3"
            _edge_voice(translated, voice, int(speech_speed), generated)
            clip = AudioSegment.from_file(generated).set_frame_rate(24000).set_channels(1)
            slot_ms = max(80, round((end - start) * 1000))
            if len(clip) > slot_ms:
                # Stretch at no more than 1.25x; if it still doesn't fit, trim the tail to avoid overlap.
                factor = min(1.25, len(clip) / slot_ms)
                tempo_filter = f"atempo={factor:.5f}"
                fitted = temp_dir / f"fit-{index:05}.wav"
                _run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-i", str(generated), "-filter:a", tempo_filter, "-t", f"{slot_ms/1000:.3f}", str(fitted)])
                clip = AudioSegment.from_file(fitted).set_frame_rate(24000).set_channels(1)[:slot_ms]
            speech_track = speech_track.overlay(clip, position=round(start * 1000))

        yield "**6/7 — Fitting timing and mixing audio…**", None, None, None, None, None
        if background:
            bed = AudioSegment.from_file(background).set_frame_rate(24000).set_channels(1)
            if len(bed) < len(speech_track):
                bed += AudioSegment.silent(duration=len(speech_track) - len(bed), frame_rate=24000)
            bed = bed[:len(speech_track)]
            # Keep source bed quieter under translated speech; preserve its original level where speech is absent.
            mixed = bed.overlay(normalize(speech_track).apply_gain(-3))
        else:
            mixed = speech_track
        mixed_path = temp_dir / "mixed.wav"
        mixed.export(mixed_path, format="wav")
        mp3_path = job_dir / f"{source_path.stem}-{target_language.lower()}-dub.mp3"
        _run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-i", str(mixed_path), "-af", "loudnorm=I=-16:TP=-1.5:LRA=11", "-codec:a", "libmp3lame", "-q:a", "2", str(mp3_path)])
        srt_path = job_dir / f"{source_path.stem}-{target_language.lower()}.srt"
        vtt_path = job_dir / f"{source_path.stem}-{target_language.lower()}.vtt"
        _write_subtitles(translated_rows, srt_path)
        _write_subtitles(translated_rows, vtt_path, vtt=True)

        yield "**7/7 — Muxing dubbed video…**", None, None, None, None, None
        mp4_path = job_dir / f"{source_path.stem}-{target_language.lower()}-dub.mp4"
        if _has_video(source_path):
            _run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-i", str(source_path), "-i", str(mp3_path), "-map", "0:v:0", "-map", "1:a:0", "-c:v", "copy", "-c:a", "aac", "-b:a", "192k", "-shortest", "-movflags", "+faststart", str(mp4_path)], timeout=1800)
        else:
            _run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-f", "lavfi", "-i", "color=c=black:s=1280x720:r=25", "-i", str(mp3_path), "-map", "0:v:0", "-map", "1:a:0", "-c:v", "libx264", "-tune", "stillimage", "-c:a", "aac", "-b:a", "192k", "-shortest", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p", "-movflags", "+faststart", str(mp4_path)], timeout=1800)

        transcript = "\n\n".join(f"{_srt_time(a)} → {_srt_time(b)}\n{src}\n→ {dst}" for a, b, src, dst in translated_rows)
        yield f"✅ **Done.** Detected source: `{detected}` · {len(translated_rows)} segments · {duration/60:.1f} minutes", mp4_path, mp3_path, srt_path, vtt_path, transcript
    except Exception as exc:
        message = str(exc)
        yield f"❌ **Dubbing failed:** {message}\n\nCheck the setup guide for FFmpeg/model requirements, then retry with a shorter file.", None, None, None, None, None
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(temp_dir, ignore_errors=True)


def build_app():
    with gr.Blocks(title="OpenDub — Free Video Dubbing", theme=gr.themes.Soft(primary_hue="indigo", neutral_hue="slate")) as demo:
        gr.Markdown("# 🎙️ OpenDub\n### Free, open-source video dubbing — runs on your machine")
        gr.Markdown("Upload media, choose one target language, and create dubbed video, MP3, SRT and VTT files. The first run downloads the selected speech and translation models. **No API keys or paid services.**")
        with gr.Row():
            media = gr.File(label="Video or audio (up to 60 minutes)", file_types=["video", "audio"], type="filepath")
            with gr.Column():
                source = gr.Dropdown(["Auto-detect", "English", "Hindi", "Kannada", "Tamil", "Telugu", "Malayalam", "Marathi", "Bengali", "Gujarati", "Punjabi", "Odia", "Urdu"], value="Auto-detect", label="Source language")
                target = gr.Dropdown(list(LANGUAGES), value="Hindi", label="Target language")
                gender = gr.Radio(["Female", "Male"], value="Female", label="Generated voice")
        with gr.Accordion("Advanced options", open=False):

# OpenDub — local video dubbing MVP

This repository currently implements **Build Step 1: a Gradio dubbing MVP**. It accepts a video/audio file, transcribes speech, translates into one selected target language, creates speech, aligns it to the original segment slots, and exports MP4, MP3, SRT, and VTT. It uses free/open-source software and does not require API keys or paid APIs.

The full multi-user Next.js + FastAPI production dashboard described in the original product brief is not part of this MVP. The local app has no user accounts or daily quota enforcement. Treat the current release as a local pipeline prototype, not a hosted service.

## Pipeline and limitations

- FFmpeg extracts audio and creates the final mux. Audio-only inputs receive a black still-video track in the MP4.
- faster-whisper provides speech transcription and timestamps. Whisper model weights download on first use.
- NLLB-200 distilled 600M translates each segment locally. Its model weights are several GB and need to download on first use; CPU translation can be slow.
- Microsoft Edge TTS is free to use through the `edge-tts` client, but it requires an internet connection and relies on Microsoft's service. It is not offline or guaranteed by an SLA.
- Demucs vocal/background separation is optional and disabled by default; enabling it downloads model weights and is slow on CPU. When enabled, the non-vocal stem is used as the music bed.
- There is no voice cloning in this MVP. No source-speaker diarization is performed; a target voice gender is selectable.
- Timing is fit to transcription slots. Very long translations are shortened and, as a last resort, trimmed to prevent overlap. Review the generated translation and subtitles before publishing.
- The UI limits media to 60 minutes. Model memory and runtime requirements vary significantly; on CPU, start with a short clip and Whisper `tiny` or `base`.

## Local setup (recommended)

Requirements: 64-bit Linux/macOS, CPython 3.11, FFmpeg (including `ffprobe`), and enough disk for model downloads. GPU is optional.

### 1. Install FFmpeg

Ubuntu/Debian:

```bash
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y ffmpeg
```

macOS with Homebrew:

```bash
brew install ffmpeg
```

Confirm both `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe` are on `PATH`:

```bash
ffmpeg -version
ffprobe -version
```

### 2. Install and start

```bash
python3.11 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
pip install -r requirements.txt
cp .env.example .env  # optional; values can also be exported in your shell
python app.py
```

Open <http://127.0.0.1:7860>. No `.env` file is needed for the default configuration. On Windows, install a CPython 3.11 environment and an FFmpeg build, then activate the venv and run `python app.py`.

### 3. Test the pipeline

1. Start with a short (10–30 second) video or audio clip with clear speech.
2. Upload it, leave source language on Auto-detect, choose a target, then click **Create dub**.
3. Wait for the first-run Whisper and NLLB model downloads; these are cached for later runs.
4. Check the MP4 and MP3, and open the SRT/VTT to verify transcript, translation, and timing.
5. Enable “Preserve background music” on a second run only after Demucs has installed successfully; CPU separation can take a while.

Generated results are stored under `outputs/<job-id>/`. Temporary working audio is removed when a job ends. Delete `outputs/` yourself when you no longer need the results.

### Useful settings

Copy `.env.example` to `.env` as a reference and export the values before launching (the app does not load dotenv automatically):

```bash
export WHISPER_DEVICE=cpu
export WHISPER_COMPUTE_TYPE=int8
export PORT=7860
python app.py
```

For CUDA, install a PyTorch build compatible with your CUDA runtime and set `WHISPER_DEVICE=cuda` and an appropriate compute type (for example `float16`). Translation uses the Transformers/PyTorch default device and can require substantial CPU/RAM. Choose `tiny` or `base` Whisper in the UI for quicker local tests.

## Docker

The image includes FFmpeg and installs the Python dependencies. Model weights are not baked into the image:

```bash
docker build -t opendub .
docker run --rm -p 7860:7860 \
  -v "$PWD/outputs:/app/outputs" \
  -v "$HOME/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface" \
  opendub
```

Then open <http://127.0.0.1:7860>. The first run downloads models into the mounted cache. Docker builds and model downloads are large.

## Free hosting notes

This pipeline is compute-heavy and uses large model downloads; free hosted tiers generally do not have enough persistent disk/RAM/CPU for reliable dubbing. A local machine is the most practical no-cost deployment.

- **Hugging Face Spaces:** create a Docker Space, use this repository's Dockerfile, and set the Space port to `7860`. Free CPU Spaces sleep and have limited resources/storage; a model load or long Demucs job may exceed those limits. Persistent storage/GPU can incur charges, so do not enable paid hardware if remaining strictly free.
- **Render free tier:** a Docker web service can be deployed from this repo, but free instances sleep and have limited memory, disk, execution time, and ephemeral storage. Long model inference is likely to be unreliable; generated files disappear on restart unless stored elsewhere. Do not use paid disks/instances if staying free.
- **Google Colab:** use a free notebook runtime, clone/copy this repository, install FFmpeg and requirements, then run `python app.py` bound to `0.0.0.0`. To expose it temporarily, use a Colab-provided share link or an open-source tunnel such as `cloudflared`; public tunneling has security/privacy implications. Free GPU availability and session lifetime are not guaranteed. Never expose private media in a public notebook/session.

This code does not configure or manage a hosted account, tunnel, or cloud resource. Review the relevant hosting and model licenses/terms before deploying.

## Structure

```text
.
├── app.py              # Gradio UI and end-to-end dubbing pipeline
├── requirements.txt
├── Dockerfile
├── .env.example
└── outputs/            # Created automatically; completed downloads
```

## License and service notes

This project is a prototype. Check the licenses of the chosen models, dependencies, and the Edge TTS service for your use case. Media processing is local except Edge TTS speech generation. The app does not upload media to a third-party API by itself, but text supplied to Edge TTS is sent to Microsoft's service.

107: def _sentence_segments(raw: list[tuple[float, float, str]], duration: float):
108:     """Merge Whisper chunks into sentence-sized dubbing slots without overlap."""
109:     merged: list[list[float | str]] = []
110:     for start, end, text in raw:
111:         start = max(0.0, min(start, duration))
112:         end = max(start + 0.05, min(end, duration))
113:         if merged and not re.search(r"[.!?。！？…]$", str(merged[-1][2])) and start - float(merged[-1][1]) < 0.8:
114:             merged[-1][1] = max(float(merged[-1][1]), end)
115:             merged[-1][2] = (str(merged[-1][2]) + " " + text).strip()
116:         else:
117:             merged.append([start, end, text])
118:     clean = []
119:     previous_end = 0.0
120:     for start, end, text in merged:
121:         start = max(float(start), previous_end)
122:         end = max(start + 0.08, float(end))
123:         end = min(duration, end)
124:         if end > start and str(text).strip():
125:             clean.append((start, end, str(text).strip()))
126:             previous_end = end

144: def _translate_piece(text: str, source_code: str, target_code: str) -> str:
145:     if not text.strip():

147:     tokenizer, model, torch = _get_translator()
148:     tokenizer.src_lang = source_code
149:     inputs = tokenizer(text, return_tensors="pt", truncation=True, max_length=512)
150:     target_id = tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids(target_code)

156: def _translate(text: str, source_code: str, target_code: str, glossary: list[str]) -> str:
157:     # Translate around glossary matches rather than asking the model to copy names/numbers.
158:     terms = [term.strip() for term in glossary if term.strip()]
159:     if not terms:
160:         return _translate_piece(text, source_code, target_code)
161:     pattern = re.compile("(" + "|".join(re.escape(t) for t in sorted(terms, key=len, reverse=True)) + ")", re.IGNORECASE)
162:     chunks = pattern.split(text)
163:     result = []
164:     for chunk in chunks:
165:         if not chunk:
166:             continue
167:         if pattern.fullmatch(chunk):
168:             result.append(chunk)
169:         else:
170:             translated = _translate_piece(chunk, source_code, target_code)
171:             result.append(translated if translated else chunk)
172:     return " ".join(part for part in result if part).strip()

20: # OpenDub — local video dubbing MVP
21: 
22: This repository currently implements **Build Step 1: a Gradio dubbing MVP**. It accepts a video/audio file, transcribes speech, translates into one selected target language, creates speech, aligns it to the original segment slots, and exports MP4, MP3, SRT, and VTT. It uses free/open-source software and does not require API keys or paid APIs.
23: 
24: The full multi-user Next.js + FastAPI production dashboard described in the original product brief is not part of this MVP. The local app has no user accounts or daily quota enforcement. Treat the current release as a local pipeline prototype, not a hosted service.
25: 
26: ## Pipeline and limitations
27: 
28: - FFmpeg extracts audio and creates the final mux. Audio-only inputs receive a black still-video track in the MP4.
29: - faster-whisper provides speech transcription and timestamps. Whisper model weights download on first use.
30: - NLLB-200 distilled 600M translates each segment locally. Its model weights are several GB and need to download on first use; CPU translation can be slow.
31: - Microsoft Edge TTS is free to use through the `edge-tts` client, but it requires an internet connection and relies on Microsoft's service. It is not offline or guaranteed by an SLA.
32: - Demucs vocal/background separation is optional and disabled by default; enabling it downloads model weights and is slow on CPU. When enabled, the non-vocal stem is used as the music bed.
33: - There is no voice cloning in this MVP. No source-speaker diarization is performed; a target voice gender is selectable.
34: - Timing is fit to transcription slots. Very long translations are shortened and, as a last resort, trimmed to prevent overlap. Review the generated translation and subtitles before publishing.
35: - The UI limits media to 60 minutes. Model memory and runtime requirements vary significantly; on CPU, start with a short clip and Whisper `tiny` or `base`.
36: 
37: ## Local setup (recommended)
38: 
39: Requirements: 64-bit Linux/macOS, CPython 3.11, FFmpeg (including `ffprobe`), and enough disk for model downloads. GPU is optional.
40: 
41: ### 1. Install FFmpeg
42: 
43: Ubuntu/Debian:
44: 
45: ```bash
46: sudo apt-get update
47: sudo apt-get install -y ffmpeg
48: ```
49: 
50: macOS with Homebrew:
51: 
52: ```bash
53: brew install ffmpeg
54: ```
55: 
56: Confirm both `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe` are on `PATH`:
57: 
58: ```bash
59: ffmpeg -version
60: ffprobe -version
61: ```
62: 
63: ### 2. Install and start
64: 
65: ```bash
66: python3.11 -m venv .venv
67: source .venv/bin/activate
68: python -m pip install --upgrade pip
69: pip install -r requirements.txt
70: cp .env.example .env  # optional; values can also be exported in your shell
71: python app.py
72: ```
73: 
74: Open <http://127.0.0.1:7860>. No `.env` file is needed for the default configuration. On Windows, install a CPython 3.11 environment and an FFmpeg build, then activate the venv and run `python app.py`.
75: 
76: ### 3. Test the pipeline
77: 
78: 1. Start with a short (10–30 second) video or audio clip with clear speech.
79: 2. Upload it, leave source language on Auto-detect, choose a target, then click **Create dub**.
80: 3. Wait for the first-run Whisper and NLLB model downloads; these are cached for later runs.
81: 4. Check the MP4 and MP3, and open the SRT/VTT to verify transcript, translation, and timing.
82: 5. Enable “Preserve background music” on a second run only after Demucs has installed successfully; CPU separation can take a while.
83: 
84: Generated results are stored under `outputs/<job-id>/`. Temporary working audio is removed when a job ends. Delete `outputs/` yourself when you no longer need the results.
85: 
86: ### Useful settings
87: 
88: Copy `.env.example` to `.env` as a reference and export the values before launching (the app does not load dotenv automatically):
89: 
90: ```bash
91: export WHISPER_DEVICE=cpu
92: export WHISPER_COMPUTE_TYPE=int8
93: export PORT=7860
94: python app.py
95: ```
96: 
97: For CUDA, install a PyTorch build compatible with your CUDA runtime and set `WHISPER_DEVICE=cuda` and an appropriate compute type (for example `float16`). Translation uses the Transformers/PyTorch default device and can require substantial CPU/RAM. Choose `tiny` or `base` Whisper in the UI for quicker local tests.
98: 
99: ## Docker
100: 
101: The image includes FFmpeg and installs the Python dependencies. Model weights are not baked into the image:
102: 
103: ```bash
104: docker build -t opendub .
105: docker run --rm -p 7860:7860 \
106:   -v "$PWD/outputs:/app/outputs" \
107:   -v "$HOME/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface" \
108:   opendub
109: ```
110: 
111: Then open <http://127.0.0.1:7860>. The first run downloads models into the mounted cache. Docker builds and model downloads are large.
112: 
113: ## Free hosting notes
114: 
115: This pipeline is compute-heavy and uses large model downloads; free hosted tiers generally do not have enough persistent disk/RAM/CPU for reliable dubbing. A local machine is the most practical no-cost deployment.
116: 
117: - **Hugging Face Spaces:** create a Docker Space, use this repository's Dockerfile, and set the Space port to `7860`. Free CPU Spaces sleep and have limited resources/storage; a model load or long Demucs job may exceed those limits. Persistent storage/GPU can incur charges, so do not enable paid hardware if remaining strictly free.
118: - **Render free tier:** a Docker web service can be deployed from this repo, but free instances sleep and have limited memory, disk, execution time, and ephemeral storage. Long model inference is likely to be unreliable; generated files disappear on restart unless stored elsewhere. Do not use paid disks/instances if staying free.
119: - **Google Colab:** use a free notebook runtime, clone/copy this repository, install FFmpeg and requirements, then run `python app.py` bound to `0.0.0.0`. To expose it temporarily, use a Colab-provided share link or an open-source tunnel such as `cloudflared`; public tunneling has security/privacy implications. Free GPU availability and session lifetime are not guaranteed. Never expose private media in a public notebook/session.
120: 
121: This code does not configure or manage a hosted account, tunnel, or cloud resource. Review the relevant hosting and model licenses/terms before deploying.
122: 
123: ## Structure
124: 
125: ```text
126: .
127: ├── app.py              # Gradio UI and end-to-end dubbing pipeline
128: ├── requirements.txt
129: ├── Dockerfile
130: ├── .env.example
131: └── outputs/            # Created automatically; completed downloads
132: ```
133: 
134: ## License and service notes
135: 
136: This project is a prototype. Check the licenses of the chosen models, dependencies, and the Edge TTS service for your use case. Media processing is local except Edge TTS speech generation. The app does not upload media to a third-party API by itself, but text supplied to Edge TTS is sent to Microsoft's service.

+# OpenDub — local video dubbing MVP
+
+This repository currently implements **Build Step 1: a Gradio dubbing MVP**. It accepts a video/audio file, transcribes speech, translates into one selected target language, creates speech, aligns it to the original segment slots, and exports MP4, MP3, SRT, and VTT. It uses free/open-source software and does not require API keys or paid APIs.
+
+The full multi-user Next.js + FastAPI production dashboard described in the original product brief is not part of this MVP. The local app has no user accounts or daily quota enforcement. Treat the current release as a local pipeline prototype, not a hosted service.
+
+## Pipeline and limitations
+
+- FFmpeg extracts audio and creates the final mux. Audio-only inputs receive a black still-video track in the MP4.
+- faster-whisper provides speech transcription and timestamps. Whisper model weights download on first use.
+- NLLB-200 distilled 600M translates each segment locally. Its model weights are several GB and need to download on first use; CPU translation can be slow.
+- Microsoft Edge TTS is free to use through the `edge-tts` client, but it requires an internet connection and relies on Microsoft's service. It is not offline or guaranteed by an SLA.
+- Demucs vocal/background separation is optional and disabled by default; enabling it downloads model weights and is slow on CPU. When enabled, the non-vocal stem is used as the music bed.
+- There is no voice cloning in this MVP. No source-speaker diarization is performed; a target voice gender is selectable.
+- Timing is fit to transcription slots. Very long translations are shortened and, as a last resort, trimmed to prevent overlap. Review the generated translation and subtitles before publishing.
+- The UI limits media to 60 minutes. Model memory and runtime requirements vary significantly; on CPU, start with a short clip and Whisper `tiny` or `base`.
+
+## Local setup (recommended)
+
+Requirements: 64-bit Linux/macOS, CPython 3.11, FFmpeg (including `ffprobe`), and enough disk for model downloads. GPU is optional.
+
+### 1. Install FFmpeg
+
+Ubuntu/Debian:
+
+```bash
+sudo apt-get update
+sudo apt-get install -y ffmpeg
+```
+
+macOS with Homebrew:
+
+```bash
+brew install ffmpeg
+```
+
+Confirm both `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe` are on `PATH`:
+
+```bash
+ffmpeg -version
+ffprobe -version
+```
+
+### 2. Install and start
+
+```bash
+python3.11 -m venv .venv
+source .venv/bin/activate
+python -m pip install --upgrade pip
+pip install -r requirements.txt
+cp .env.example .env  # optional; values can also be exported in your shell
+python app.py
+```
+
+Open <http://127.0.0.1:7860>. No `.env` file is needed for the default configuration. On Windows, install a CPython 3.11 environment and an FFmpeg build, then activate the venv and run `python app.py`.
+
+### 3. Test the pipeline
+
+1. Start with a short (10–30 second) video or audio clip with clear speech.
+2. Upload it, leave source language on Auto-detect, choose a target, then click **Create dub**.
+3. Wait for the first-run Whisper and NLLB model downloads; these are cached for later runs.
+4. Check the MP4 and MP3, and open the SRT/VTT to verify transcript, translation, and timing.
+5. Enable “Preserve background music” on a second run only after Demucs has installed successfully; CPU separation can take a while.
+
+Generated results are stored under `outputs/<job-id>/`. Temporary working audio is removed when a job ends. Delete `outputs/` yourself when you no longer need the results.
+
+### Useful settings
+
+Copy `.env.example` to `.env` as a reference and export the values before launching (the app does not load dotenv automatically):
+
+```bash
+export WHISPER_DEVICE=cpu
+export WHISPER_COMPUTE_TYPE=int8
+export PORT=7860
+python app.py
+```
+
+For CUDA, install a PyTorch build compatible with your CUDA runtime and set `WHISPER_DEVICE=cuda` and an appropriate compute type (for example `float16`). Translation uses the Transformers/PyTorch default device and can require substantial CPU/RAM. Choose `tiny` or `base` Whisper in the UI for quicker local tests.
+
+## Local FastAPI job API (prototype)
+
+A separate FastAPI service wraps the same dubbing pipeline with an in-process, single-worker queue. It accepts multipart uploads up to 2 GB, returns a job ID, exposes status/progress, and provides MP4/MP3/SRT/VTT download routes. Jobs and queue state are held in memory and disappear when the process restarts; outputs remain under `outputs/`.
+
+Start it from the activated environment after installing requirements:
+
+```bash
+python api.py
+```
+
+Open <http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs> for the interactive API documentation. The main routes are `POST /api/jobs`, `GET /api/jobs/{job_id}`, and `GET /api/jobs/{job_id}/files/{video|audio|srt|vtt}`. The upload form fields use the same language, voice, glossary, speed, and Whisper choices as the Gradio app.
+
+This is still a local prototype, **not a secure public multi-user service**: it has no authentication, durable job store, daily quota enforcement, or cross-process worker. Keep the default localhost binding. Before exposing it publicly, add authentication, request/rate limits, durable queue/storage, and deployment-specific upload limits.
+
+## Docker
+
+The image includes FFmpeg and installs the Python dependencies. Model weights are not baked into the image:
+
+```bash
+docker build -t opendub .
+docker run --rm -p 7860:7860 \
+  -v "$PWD/outputs:/app/outputs" \
+  -v "$HOME/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface" \
+  opendub
+```
+
+Then open <http://127.0.0.1:7860>. The first run downloads models into the mounted cache. Docker builds and model downloads are large.
+
+## Free hosting notes
+
+This pipeline is compute-heavy and uses large model downloads; free hosted tiers generally do not have enough persistent disk/RAM/CPU for reliable dubbing. A local machine is the most practical no-cost deployment.
+
+- **Hugging Face Spaces:** create a Docker Space, use this repository's Dockerfile, and set the Space port to `7860`. Free CPU Spaces sleep and have limited resources/storage; a model load or long Demucs job may exceed those limits. Persistent storage/GPU can incur charges, so do not enable paid hardware if remaining strictly free.
+- **Render free tier:** a Docker web service can be deployed from this repo, but free instances sleep and have limited memory, disk, execution time, and ephemeral storage. Long model inference is likely to be unreliable; generated files disappear on restart unless stored elsewhere. Do not use paid disks/instances if staying free.
+- **Google Colab:** use a free notebook runtime, clone/copy this repository, install FFmpeg and requirements, then run `python app.py` bound to `0.0.0.0`. To expose it temporarily, use a Colab-provided share link or an open-source tunnel such as `cloudflared`; public tunneling has security/privacy implications. Free GPU availability and session lifetime are not guaranteed. Never expose private media in a public notebook/session.
+
+This code does not configure or manage a hosted account, tunnel, or cloud resource. Review the relevant hosting and model licenses/terms before deploying.

# OpenDub — local video dubbing MVP

The core product currently implements **Build Step 1: a Gradio dubbing MVP**. It accepts a video/audio file, transcribes speech, translates into one selected target language, creates speech, aligns it to the original segment slots, and exports MP4, MP3, SRT, and VTT. A separate local FastAPI job API is also available as an early backend step. The stack uses free/open-source software and does not require API keys or paid APIs.

The full multi-user Next.js dashboard and production backend described in the original product brief are not part of this prototype. There are no user accounts, durable jobs, or daily quota enforcement. Treat the current release as a local pipeline prototype, not a hosted service.

## Pipeline and limitations

- FFmpeg extracts audio and creates the final mux. Audio-only inputs receive a black still-video track in the MP4.
- faster-whisper provides speech transcription and timestamps. Whisper model weights download on first use.
- NLLB-200 distilled 600M translates each segment locally. Its model weights are several GB and need to download on first use; CPU translation can be slow.
- Microsoft Edge TTS is free to use through the `edge-tts` client, but it requires an internet connection and relies on Microsoft's service. It is not offline or guaranteed by an SLA.
- Demucs vocal/background separation is optional and disabled by default; enabling it downloads model weights and is slow on CPU. When enabled, the non-vocal stem is used as the music bed.
- There is no voice cloning in this MVP. No source-speaker diarization is performed; a target voice gender is selectable.
- Timing is fit to transcription slots. Very long translations are shortened and, as a last resort, trimmed to prevent overlap. Review the generated translation and subtitles before publishing.
- The UI limits media to 60 minutes. Model memory and runtime requirements vary significantly; on CPU, start with a short clip and Whisper `tiny` or `base`.
